Definition: from G2370; an aroma, i.e. fragrant powder burnt in religious service; by implication, the burning itself:--incense, odour.
BiblicalUsage: The word thymíama carries the sense of incense. In Luke 1:10, the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the time of incense. Wherever it appears, the word means this and not something vaguer.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that prayer rises to God like incense, and He does not despise the offering of a sincere heart. That is why thymíama stays with me long after the verse is closed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
